svg.title: Five recurring AI-on-RFID failure modes paired with their preventions
svg.desc: Five failure-and-prevention pairs. One: treating RFID as a reporting feed, not an event stream — nightly snapshots miss the in-day signal, slow analytics rather than AI; prevented by standing up the streaming layer (Kafka, Kinesis, Impinj ItemSense or Zebra Savanna) before the model. Two: skipping the data-quality bake-off — a 99% read-rate store and an 88% store train wildly different models; prevented by a 30-day accuracy audit per store using Auburn RFID Lab methodology. Three: leaving the markdown model unsupervised — a misconfigured model can torch margin in 48 hours; prevented by human-in-the-loop on price actions above a set threshold for at least the first two seasons. Four: the cross-channel data gap — a store-only view recommends reorders that never arrive in time; prevented by federating the EPCIS 2.0 event layer across stores, DCs, in-transit and store-to-store before scaling. Five: no baseline for the ROI claim — without a matched-pair store control the number is indefensible to the CFO; prevented by baking the matched-pair design into the pilot before procurement signs, because retro-fitting after launch is statistically impossible.
svg.text: THE WRECKAGE, CATALOGUED
Never the chip: five failure modes, five preventions

Learning these here is cheaper than learning them in production — where the tuition is billed in margin.
